item.description:
Awakening Asheville You do not have to walk this path alone. In fact, this journey is that much more rich and enjoyable when traversed with others. Groups Openings
First Saturday of each month – mornings at 10:30 am Eastern Led by Buddhist teacher Ronya Banks, this group meets once a month, for an hour and a half.
Group Meeting Includes: Group Discussion and Sharing Instruction on Dharma/Buddhist Principles Guided Meditation Meditation Instruction Connecting with Other Practitioners Most people on a spiritual journey find it supportive, often even necessary to get the regular support of a meditation teacher, as well as the mutuality and connection with other meditation practitioners on this path.
This monthly group affords you with the opportunity to connect with a teacher and other like-minded people, wherein you will all boldly delve deeply into different ways of approaching your formal and informal mindfulness practices through the lens of the Buddhist teachings.

item.title: Sadie Hawkins Day — Fri Nov 13, 4:00 PM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends **Sadie Hawkins Day** Where: anywhere ya kin find a loose single quaverin’ boy. **Refer to the ‘usual’ HFF announcements for details of time & place.** https://nationaltoday.com/sadie-hawkins-day/ History of Sadie Hawkins Day The tradition stems from a plot line in American cartoonist Al Capp’s (1909-1979) comic strip, “Li’l Abner,” which, unlike most comic strips of the time, was set in the American South, and not Northeastern cities and suburbs. The story — one reviled by modern feminists — involved a rich man’s daughter named Sadie Hawkins in the fictional town of Dogpatch, Kentucky, who was so ‘homely’ that she was still unmarried at 35. Her worried father then gathered all the bachelors of the town together and set up a sort of race, with the men running ahead of Sadie. The one she finally caught would have to marry her. item.title: John Rock Loop Hike — Sun Nov 15, 9:00 AM
item.description:
WNC Sierra Club Join the WNC Sierra Club for a beautiful hike in the Pisgah National Forest. The John Rock Loop hike features around 1,100 feet of elevation gain up to a scenic overlook where we will have a snack and rest. This hike is about 5.9 miles in length and will take us approximately 3-4 hours. Be prepared for elevation gain and creek crossings. Make sure to pack food and water to stay nourished and hydrated! Wear gear that you are comfortable hiking in and good shoes. It is also a good idea to have rain gear just to be safe. If you are feeling unwell and/or have a fever, please help us to keep everyone safe and healthy by waiting for the next outing. Families, friends, and pets are all welcome. An adult must accompany all children. All dogs must remain on a leash and be friendly to all.
Please register using this [Link to John Rock Loop Registration.](https://act.sierraclub.org/events/details?formcampaignid=701Po00002IzggXIAR&_gl=1*101y2wv*_gcl_au*MTE0NzgwMjQ3Ni4xNzkwNjQ0NDE2

item.title: The Body of the Golem: A Life in Portraiture — Sun Nov 15, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Artist and writer Riva Lehrer brings together portraiture, Jewish tradition, disability, and the figure of the golem for the 2026 Phyllis Freed Sollod Memorial Lecture in the Mountain View Room of the Sherrill Center. Through art and storytelling, Lehrer explores who gets labeled “monstrous,” who has the power to define that label, and what becomes possible when people claim their own bodies and identities. This lecture is sponsored by the Center for Jewish Studies. The event is free and open to the public. Accessibility UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

The mind is rich with creative power. Every day, it conceives a multitude of realities. While these experiences may bring us a sense of joy and freedom, they can also be limiting, disruptive and even painful. Buddha taught us how to use our imagination to see behind our ordinary thinking, moving us into extraordinary realms of possibility. item.title: The Next Five: Build ADN’s 2027 Together — Tue Dec 1, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Digital Nomads Ever wondered how AVL Digital Nomads actually works, who makes it happen, and where it’s headed next? Come find out, and help decide.
ADN has almost 6,000 members and zero employees. Every social, lunch, book club, and workshop on our calendar exists because a nomad decided it should. This evening is a look behind the curtain: where we’ve been, where we’re going, and the many ways to be part of it. It’s built as much for people who joined this year as for longtime regulars.
We’re gathering where ADN began in 2021: Wedge Brewing at Foundation, in the new community room they built after Helene. It felt like the right place to start the next chapter.
**What happens**
* **Where ADN is headed:** A short, honest look at the mission and what’s next. * **“My First Event” stories:** Longtime organizers share how they got started, mishaps included. * **The Idea Wall:** Ideas from RSVPs go up on the wall. Add yours and vote with dot stickers. Have an idea already? Share it
